newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro stocks hit records, oil stays strong.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro stocks hit records, oil stays strong.

text.p: A record close on Wall Street, the world's dominant stock market, helped propel the London and Frankfurt bourses to new peaks in morning trading on Tuesday.
World oil prices were also buoyant, trading near six-year highs after resuming an advance which has boosted them by 40 percent in the last four months.
On the foreign exchanges the dollar hit a 33-month high against the yen and a four-month high against the mark, while the pound rose generally, aided by the rally in share prices and dearer oil.

On Monday, the Dow Jones industrial average ended above 6,000 for the first time, cheered by a healthy U.S. economic outlook, a jump in oil prices, which ignited oil shares, and good results from Chrysler.
The 30-share Dow jumped 40.62 points to 6,010.00. In a dizzying rise, it soared through 5,000 only last November, nine months after topping 4,000.

London's stock market, Europe's busiest, had already breached the 4,000 mark on the FTSE 100 share index and made further progress in early trading, supported by higher bond prices and news of an agreed bid for international exhibitions group Blenheim.
"The market is in very good heart," said one senior trader. "Blenheim added fuel to the fire and the feeling is there are other bids still in the pipeline," another added.
"Breaking the 4,100 level is a real possibility this week," said one dealer. "There's no reason to start selling right now... even if you are bearish on the market," he added.
London shares have tagged along with U.S. markets since late July amid indications that U.S. interest rates, a key influence on other markets, were not likely to rise in the near future.
Germany's DAX index opened at a record high above 2,700 and added to its gains, boosted by Wall Street's close, higher bonds and strength in the dollar -- good news for German exporters.
French shares, meanwhile, raced to a new high for the year at midsession, led by gains in oil stocks.

Traders said a 40 percent jump in quarterly profits of computer chip giant Intel, announced after Monday's New York close, could give a further boost to shares. Technology stocks led most other U.S. equities higher in London on Tuesday.
But they said all eyes would be on how Wall Street performed when it reopened as Monday's gains were won in muted trading, when the U.S. bond market was shut for the Columbus Day holiday.
Investors might also await British and U.S. economic figures later in the week, particularly U.S. September consumer price (CPI) data on Wednesday.
"U.S. CPI is the big one," said one London trader. "People will not want to stick their neck out too much ahead of that."

Soaring oil prices weakened the yen, in view of Japan's dependence on imported oil, while helping to send the pound to 21-month highs against the mark, 11-month peaks versus the dollar and three-year highs against the yen.
London November futures for international benchmark North Sea Brent blend crude were up 17 cents a barrel at $25.03 soon after midday after adding 88 cents on Monday to set a new post-Gulf War high.
"Sterling's broken all our near-term targets and it could go a lot further, possibly to 2.48 marks," said a U.S. bank trader.
The yen also attracted some uncertainty ahead of Sunday's Japanese general election.
CURRENCIES AT 1115 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5370 marks and 112.20 yen, compared with 1.5293 and 111.60 in late European business on Monday. The pound gained to $1.5825 and 2.4325 marks from $1.5805 and 2.4174.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1115 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 21.4 points at 4,060.1, a record high.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was 34.76 ahead at 2,728.64, also a record.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was 25.38 higher at 2,169.00, just below a year high around 2,170 hit earlier.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold traded around $381.15 an ounce after being fixed at $381 in the morning, compared with Monday's London close of $381.65 and afternoon fix of $380.90. Silver slipped three cents to $5.02.
